notes:
VERDICT: BLOCKED. Prediction confirmed exactly: bulk_restore_archived_test_plans returns the identical 404 {success:false, errors:'Feature not available'} as its archive sibling, on the first and only attempt. One attempt was enough — the error is deterministic and contract-documented, and three other capabilities scoped to this exact project (bulk_archive_test_plans, list_archived_test_plans, get_archived_test_plan_count) all independently hit the same 404 in prior probes, so this is not a fluke or a payload problem. No 200 was ever returned, so declared_missing/undeclared_returned stay empty (never diff an error body against the success schema).

ONE FLAG, WHOLE PAIR: this cleanly confirms the single group feature flag disables both halves of test-plan archiving — archive AND un-archive/restore — for this preprod group/project. There is no asymmetry where a caller could restore something they can't archive; both directions are equally unreachable.

CONTRAST WITH TEST-CASE ARCHIVING: test-*case* archiving is NOT gated the same way — bulk_archive_test_cases_by_project and bulk_restore_archived_test_cases both worked live (four cases archived and cleanly restored). So this feature flag is specific to test *plans*; it does not touch the equivalent test-case flow at all. Worth stating explicitly as a scoping fact about the flag, not a general 'archiving is broken here' claim.

CONTRACT ASYMMETRY WORTH NOTING: bulk_restore_archived_test_plans's own describeCapability response DOES declare this 404 explicitly in its response schema ('Test-plan archiving is not enabled for this group'). Per the task brief, the archive sibling's declared error surface did NOT include this 404 — so the two capabilities in the same undo pair document their shared failure mode inconsistently: the restore side owns up to it in its contract, the archive side doesn't. That is itself a small drift worth flagging to whoever authored the archive capability's error responses.

NO TARGET, TWO INDEPENDENT REASONS: no archived test plan exists to restore, and there is also no way to discover one even if it existed. (1) list_test_plans_by_integer_id's own guidance states archived plans never appear in that listing under any filter. (2) The dedicated archived-plans listing (list_archived_test_plans) and count (get_archived_test_plan_count) are themselves both gated 404 by the same flag, per prior probes on this same project. So the capability is unreachable for two compounding reasons: the flag blocks the restore call itself, AND even the id-discovery path for a target is blocked by the same flag. Sent our disposable TP-1632 (48319, active, not archived) as the id purely to exercise the route; TP-1616 (48283) and the other 28 pre-existing plans were never referenced.

SENDING A NON-ARCHIVED ID: TP-1632 is active, not archived, so this attempt also tested how the route responds to an id that isn't archived — but the feature-flag gate fires before any id-validity logic runs, so nothing was learned about that specific behavior (no 'plan is not archived' style response was reached; the flag masks it entirely).

SELECT_ALL / FOOTGUN CHECK: describeCapability shows exactly one body field, test_plan_ids (a plain integer array) — no select_all or de_selected_ids parameter exists on this capability, matching its archive sibling. No footgun to avoid here.

NAME-INVITES-WRONG-MODEL, FOURTH INSTANCE: 'retrieve' in the name strongly suggests a read, but this is a write (mode: 'write') that restores/un-archives plans — the exact same pattern already seen in bulk_set_test_case_assignee_in_run, delete_folder_and_subtree, and bulk_restore_archived_test_cases. This is a fourth confirmed case of a capability name inviting the wrong operation model, worth flagging as a recurring naming-convention problem across this index rather than a one-off.

NOT EXERCISED (and why): the synchronous vs. async (>30 ids) response split, the to_i id-coercion/zero-drop behavior, and the 400 'Please provide test plan ids' empty-array path were all left unexercised — the feature-flag gate fires before any of that request-shape logic can run, so none of it is reachable in this environment regardless of payload.
